findings.evidence: AE130 is called once per scene from B7A8A. Preserve all six spring fields and lifetime at original rule cadence; apply a sampled local shake to both newly rebuilt matrices each scene. Original ADDD0 impulse units and callers remain unchanged. ADE60/ADFC0/B7350 reset five bounded native histories. Spring-only private original previews cannot draw, change duration or tail-reset the real global camera. Full whole-tick calls retain original CPU behavior.

Mode5 shares camera+30 between IIR history and rendered angle. Preserve its original integer SAR, pause and immediate-max geometry branches; commit state only at original rule ticks and sample a prospective original map for each scene. A transient direct-max display cannot alter later committed rules. Existing ADFC0/B7350 lifecycles reset five bounded histories; no new hook runs in other view modes. Original geometry/FPATAN remains unchanged.

Original B74C0 mode2/3 recentering runs after controller dispatch on every scene; its fixed signed1/240 steps therefore accelerated with rendering rate. Scale only those four original add/sub operands by elapsed scene ticks. Preserve the original zero clamps, view modes, pause behavior and exact whole-tick arithmetic. FOV response B7945/B794A is separate open research.

200F0/202F0 allocate size+0x23, align the returned pointer to32 bytes and keep the original pointer atresult-4;20150/20320 free that saved pointer.6D38E0 and per-heap6D36E4 count outstanding allocations.21420 reserves pages or a0x4000-byte pool, storing size atrecord+1C, stride+10 and capacity+14.215D0 reserves element counts at+18 and increments pool references+0C;215A0/216E0 decrement references and destroy the pool at zero.6D3A50 totals bytes,6D3A54 pools and6D3A5C wrapper objects. These counters follow allocation/release calls, not scene time. Complete bounded original analyses: timing/research/reference-counters/original. Caller timing, scheduling and resource-service behavior retain their separate coverage obligations.

Complete28AB0 multiplies the current6DD5A0 affine matrix by the supplied3x4 matrix;28B80/28C30 compose a supplied translation,28CE0/28D90 subtract it, and28E40/28E90 apply supplied axis/uniform scale.294A0/29550/29600 rotate matrix columns using their supplied sine/cosine pair, including drawing/view callers that reset the transform first.29E70 multiplies four quaternion components by the inverse of their norm, falling back to1 near zero. These are geometry operations with caller-supplied transforms, not elapsed counters or velocities. Timing belongs to the specific producer/caller; scaling these shared primitives would also scale absolute drawing geometry. Bounded complete original analyses: timing/research/matrix-primitives/original. Caller timing, scheduling and resource-service behavior retain their separate coverage obligations.

B3BA0 couples target/lookahead ownership, signed yaw/pitch responses and bank decay. Commit the complete original camera rule once per tick. Evaluate an original next rule on a private28C-byte camera record for the scene pose, preserving shared matrix/counters and guest floating state; camera+9C..B0 remain original committed history. Five fixed record lifecycles discard samples on reset. Whole-tick yaw/bank bytes, both signs,50/60 clocks, pause and reset are pinned. Scene drawing uses a private ball copy for a bounded one-remaining-tick velocity forecast, never changing committed inputs. Current target translation follows the actual ball; only relative orbit and angles are sampled. Paired original-AOT ownership research separately covers acceleration, reversal and teleport, without claiming future-impact prediction.

68840 first copies source X/Y into its outputs, then applies half/full width and height alignment offsets. 68B60 advances a glyph cursor by glyph width; 68E00 handles newline, tab and spacing. 691C0 applies sprite-anchor alignment and normalizes the alignment flags before drawing its nine slices. 6A1E0 drains the 28-byte draw queue, decrementing 7196E8 once per submitted record, then clears it. These are geometry and queue bookkeeping, not elapsed time. Bounded original analyses: timing/research/hud-counters/original.

Shared integer increment now uses the actual previous phase. Original goal-flight path and independent quaternion rule reproduce the rounding failure at 75/1000 Hz and irregular intervals; other users share the helper but retain their own gameplay coverage obligations.
Positive signed WORLD+1C duration is a rule counter. Only its decrement is gated; traversal, responses and matrix construction remain per scene.

The original /4 response acts on signed angles. Fractional exponential response carries angle precision in the four verified WORLD records; both controllers are checked against independent formulas and original 60 Hz bytes.

Previous scaling at A7D1B/A7D2E still rounded signed tilt after every small step, losing up to 25.8 angle units in five ticks at 1000 Hz. Carry precision at the final store and invalidate it on original per-record initialization or transition to the vector/scripted controller; retain original full-tick bytes.

Compose original .2 response and .8 decay before fractional iteration. Preserve original full-tick conversions; reset fractional history at the original four-record initializer. Numeric scope covers neutral/clamped input, opposite signs, pause and reset.
Use only the active part of an interval for shrinking; original expiry tick holds radius, then the trailing phase begins recovery. Every sample through expiry is checked.

13B70 is the INFO initializer, reached via the event lifecycle. Its conditional 6C7D2C increment accompanies course initialization, not elapsed scene time. Bounded original analysis: timing/research/original/0x00013B70.json.
1F4C0 adjusts current draw-context +F8. 5A5A0 calls it with +0.5, draws the queue, then calls -0.5: a scoped drawing offset, not a velocity. Leave the original arithmetic intact.

1F4E0/1F570/1F660 clamp the computed draw depth bucket to count minus one. At 531AA..531CB the caller computes the bucket, reserves 0x14 bytes via 1F7E0 and inserts the packet via 1F770, which increments the draw-context count. 1F820 clears the list/count and restores the arena cursor and free bytes. None of these fields measure elapsed time.

1DD10 mixes recurring drawing with 6D010C duration clamped to 0..8; alpha is count*0.1 at 1DDA5. Advance duration on rule ticks and sample alpha per scene, including the first opening fraction. Prefix probes stop explicitly at 74F10, before drawing; original 60 Hz counter and alpha bytes are pinned.

97E00 advances the elapsed clock on rule ticks and samples its original pre-increment weight per scene. At expiry the secondary clip flag and both clocks clear on the original tick. 9C540 and 9AED0 use the same active interval when selecting a clip or querying completion. Prefix probes pin weights, clock/flag bytes and the pending-clip branch; the CPU diagnostic checks the query.

97D20 keeps its full rule-tick increment for both bounds and wrap distance. 99300 samples the phase once per clip before its 98B50 bone loop. At high refresh the same pre-advance interval survives into intermediate scenes; loop counters and completion stay on the original rule. Prefix probes cover both pose inputs, forward and reverse restart, and one-shot hold. CPU diagnostics separately exercise the end queries.

9ADE0 is an explicit seek even when the requested float equals the advanced playhead. It invalidates the prior sample. 98920 copies the outgoing track to the secondary blend slot and transfers its pose interval before 978E0 initializes the new primary track.

9C540 and 94F60 mix pose work with original PRNG rolls, cue state transitions and duration updates. Keep each cue's rolls, transitions, increments and decrements on rule ticks. Resume through the original saved-register cleanup and 98B20 model call. Captured-model prefixes check seed, cue start, expiry, misses and model argument across the schedule matrix.

The original comparison and the signed step both use the three-unit 347B84 constant. Scale both by the scene interval in the menu and actor paths, so the target is reached at the same elapsed time. Captured-model prefixes cover both signs, intermediate samples and exact endpoint bytes.

6BB60 advances its reveal clock and dispatches 6B8F0 once per original rule tick after the delay. The 0.1 and 0.15 scale and appearance gains compose across rendered scenes. Full calls with a real glyph queue check the original reveal ticks, cursor, terminator, pause and both scale paths.

6AC40 clamps a parsed style index. 6B8F0 moves its ring indices, line number and width per parsed token. 6A850 counts glyphs before a delay escape; 6BA3A transitions the delay over those glyphs. The reveal caller owns elapsed time and these per-token operations retain their original arithmetic.

The verified 6BB60 rule advances placement and the signed angular spring together. Fractional scenes evaluate the original placement against a private text-box copy, then sample that result for 6B520 drawing. The guest pose and the old relative vector used by the next rule are unchanged by drawing. Probes preserve detached pause/resume and captured anchored placement, velocity and roll through four original ticks.

cases.name: dialog-closing

cases.name: dialog-clamped
